title: Beach and Seaside Days Out: Rock Pools, Fossils, Piers
description: Family seaside days out: rock pooling, fossil hunting on the Jurassic Coast, classic piers and arcades, and staying safe with lifeguards and beach flags.
intro: Sandcastles, rock pools, fish and chips and a go on the 2p machines. The seaside is the original family day out, and much of it is free.

image.alt: A family walking on the beach holding hands

blocks.title: Scout’s seaside verdict
blocks.text: Choose a lifeguarded beach, swim between the red and yellow flags, and check the tide times before rock pooling or fossil hunting.

sections.html: In the UK, lifeguarded beaches use red and yellow flags to mark the safest area to swim. Never swim at a red flag. If someone is in trouble in the water, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard. Read beach safety for families and the rock pooling guide.

faqs.q: What do the red and yellow flags mean on a beach?
faqs.a: They mark an area patrolled by lifeguards and the safest place to swim and bodyboard. Always swim between them.
